Make clicking actually land: page segmentation, and a stricter match

click_text had never run end to end. Driving it against a real browser found
two things, both of which made it click confidently in the wrong place.

tesseract was reading with --psm 6, "a single uniform block of text", copied
from omarchy-capture-text where a human has dragged a box around a paragraph.
A screen is not that — it is a bar, a sidebar, tabs and a page in columns — and
psm 6 read straight past the tab row of a GitHub pull request. psm 3 finds it
and reads more of everything else.

And a run qualified on half its words, so a two-word target passed on one:
asked for "Files changed" it matched the words "changed files" in the body
prose and clicked there. Every word is now required, with one word of slack
for phrases long enough that OCR will reliably mangle one.

Verified end to end: click_text("Discussions") moved the pointer to the words
on screen, clicked, and the browser navigated — title went from the pull
request to "omacom/omarchy · Discussions".

Also: ydotool's own `mousemove --absolute` lands at twice the requested
coordinates on this display, so positioning stays with hl.dsp.cursor.move and
ydotool is only asked to press the button.
